notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a complete-looking seven-page primary research article, with title Behavioral Priming: It’s all in the Mind, but Whose Mind? (title contains a duplicated W in extraction), authors Stéphane Doyen, Olivier Klein, Cora-Lise Pichon and Axel Cleeremans, PLoS ONE 7(1), e29081 (2012), DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0029081 in its citation, matching the assigned replication reference. Contains Methods, Results, Discussion and references, rather than abstract-only material. No PDF was supplied, so no rendering was possible. Target is established from Experiment 1 and the p. 3 walking-speed replication test, independently of row order or numeric correspondence. Canonical text prints g2 = .01; retain this literal metric token without claiming eta-squared versus partial eta-squared identity. Canonical text prints F (1, 119),1; comma is preserved verbatim and appears to represent a less-than sign in extraction. No numerical p or p-bound is given for this walking-speed test; do not borrow p = 0.023 from the distinct awareness chi-squared test. N = 120 is a candidate Experiment 1 participation/sample count (Methods and Discussion), not extracted as model analytic N; no N is inferred from degrees of freedom and no group sum is calculated. Original and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
